events.title: Portuguese occupation
hints: A fleet from Hormuz seized an island group famed for pearls in 1521.
The Portuguese built a fort and ran the pearl trade through puppet governors.
A revolt in 1602 and Persian forces ended their rule.
events.summary: Portugal took the islands in 1521 from the Jabrid emirate of al-Hasa, strengthening the Bahrain Fort and taxing the pearl trade. Local resentment and Safavid pressure ended Portuguese control in 1602.

events.title: Persian rule
hints: A Persian shah's forces took the islands in 1602.
Local governors ruled for the Safavids, with a brief Omani occupation in the 1700s.
The Al Khalifa family from the mainland took the islands in 1783.
events.summary: Safavid Persia took the islands in 1602 and ruled them through governors, with interruptions including an Omani occupation in 1717-1736 and Nader Shah's reconquest in 1736. The Al Khalifa family expelled the last Persian-appointed governor in 1783.

events.title: British protection and the Exclusive Agreement
hints: In 1820 the ruler signed a treaty of peace with a naval power that patrolled the Gulf.
An 1892 Exclusive Agreement bound the ruler not to deal with other powers without consent.
The first Gulf oil well came in 1932 and independence in 1971.
events.summary: Bahrain signed the 1820 General Maritime Treaty with Britain, and the 1861 and 1892 agreements placed its foreign affairs under British control. A British political agent dominated administration. Oil was found in 1932, and Britain withdrew in 1971.
events.quip: A protectorate where the ruler was free to do anything except decide anything.
